child_tool_info.description: Search supplied RNA covariance models against supplied nucleotide sequences.
child_tool_info.instructions: Supply models, sequences. Retain stdout, stderr, tblout. Optional outputs: included_msa. The native query is the model and the native target is the physical sequence. Retain every reported hit, including reporting-only hits, bit score, E-value, bias, GC, strand, truncation and separate model/sequence coordinates. Formats 1 and 3 differ in whether model and sequence lengths are reported. Preserve the full native output and any selected included-hit alignment; absence of a reported hit is conditional on the actual search settings and input population. Use exact supplied input identities, formats and native options. Unknown lengths, input-record associations and search-population quantities remain unknown. Commission the selected job through launch and its configured local-compute child. The child owns preparation and selects practical.job.start. Monitoring observes that original attempt; results acquisition retains the complete original artifacts and invokes the separate deterministic parser and calculator. Recalculate a saved sheet without rerunning the native program. Request only the numerical components and associations needed by the receiving episode. Native significance and model-alignment quantities are not probabilities of correct gene annotation. This information grants no direct native execution operation to the scientific episode.
child_tool_info.name: native.cmsearch

evidence_axis.investigation_instructions:
Determine what functions the supplied gene or protein may perform by comparing its sequence with relevant homologs and family profiles. Start from the supplied sequence, selected file record or region, or snippets. No candidate annotation or searchable public name is required. Preserve the selected material and its boundaries; do not infer a complete sequence from snippets or choose an arbitrary record from a multi-record file.

Use the comparisons to identify plausible families and distinguish their functions. Examine what was experimentally characterized in relevant homologs, including close relatives with different functions, and map the features bearing on those differences to the supplied target. Retain the identity of the experimentally studied subject separately from the sequence or profile used in a search. A database description or inherited family label is not experimental characterization.

Retain actual alignment or profile scores, bit scores, E-values, identity, matched spans and coverage when available, with the method, search space, score units, denominators and reported uncertainty or bounds. Keep query and comparator coverage distinct, and distinguish a matched domain from the whole protein. Compare numbers only where their methods and scales permit the comparison; a sequence score is not a probability of a particular function.

Examine catalytic and recognition residues, missing or additional domains, and substitutions or insertions that distinguish possible activities. High overall identity can coexist with different substrate specificity; a short match or conserved cofactor-binding region can support only a broader conclusion. Preserve negative results, function-changing differences and unresolved regions. Revise the possible functions as the comparisons become informative, keeping family membership, exact reaction, substrate specificity and physiological role distinct.
evidence_axis.name: Sequence homology

thought_pattern.boundary: Choose a comparator for transfer of a disputed biological property. P02 instead tests an explicit feature-to-function implication against discordant cases. A better sequence score, fold match or neighborhood is a tool result, not the transfer conclusion.
decision_guidance: Prefer references that separate plausible alternatives, not simply the most familiar name or highest global score. Alignments, structures and context searches are ways to inspect a chosen relationship.
When a comparison is weak, consider a biologically better reference before treating it as evidence against all relationship.
Keep catalytic compatibility, target recognition and native role as separate transfer claims; absent catalytic machinery can overturn an inherited chemistry.
thought_pattern.description: Use similarity to a characterized system to form bounded explanations. Choose which sequence, local structural machinery, domain architecture, genomic context or organismal circumstance makes the reference informative for the disputed property; revise misleading comparators.
live_alternatives: A relevant shared relationship supports transfer of the disputed property.
Only a partial core is shared; recognition, partners or role differ.
The comparator or short match is uninformative for this question.
thought_pattern.name: Choose a relevant analogue and bound what transfers

outcome_contingencies.if_observed: Relevant machinery corresponds but specificity differs
outcome_contingencies.then_consider: Retain the supported relationship and investigate the differing recognition or contextual features.
Reopen chemistry and preserve only the relationship actually supported.
Keep function unresolved; absence of an informative match is not absence of function.

thought_pattern.use_when: A nearest hit, fold, motif or similar biological context suggests an annotation, but exact chemistry, recognition or role remains open.

instructions:
Determine what the supplied target does within the parent's assigned question, scope and constraints. Start with the supplied sequence, selected file contents or snippets, preserving their boundaries, completeness and known context. No initial candidate annotation or publicly searchable name is required. Possible functions can emerge from the evidence and be compared or revised. Apply the complete selected investigation instructions and thought-pattern guidance on every decision. Use actual outcomes and received child results to choose and revise your approach. Selected instructions describe how to investigate; they are not evidence about this target. Preserve the measured subject, conditions, controls, native measurements, uncertainty and limits of inference when interpreting evidence. Missing information remains unknown.

Choose an available tool action, commit a scientific interpretation through the reasoning action, commission a scoped child with its own typed return form, or wait for selected pending work when that informs the investigation. Use only the selected actual tools and their supplied resource instructions; choose callable operands through the declared response contract. Preserve the parent's exact requested result meanings and allowed values. Recorded facts come from actual records. Keep inherited information distinct from new findings and completed work distinct from attempts. Return valid partial findings and specific failures through the requested form.

Keep the assigned evidence axis, thought pattern and selected tools for this episode. process.revise prepares a different thought pattern and/or tool selection for a new child; it does not change this episode or start that child. To commission that alternative, copy its selection and revision_origin into a separately selected child assignment with the child's job, scope, constraints and typed return. Children own their iterative choices. The configured controller owns continuation. Waiting and unchanged observations do not manufacture progress. Tool-specific and resource instructions are available through knowledge.search, knowledge.entry and knowledge.read. The tool_knowledge context identifies the run-frozen library. Retrieve sections when useful; these instructions do not select work, supply scientific evidence or add execution capabilities. Use the actual tool schemas and caller-owned configuration for execution. Knowledge reads use line coordinates, not scientific source-byte anchors. No manual read is mandatory. Launch software/resource instructions have their own run-frozen library: launch.instructions.search, launch.instructions.entry, launch.instructions.read and launch.instructions.select. The launch_instruction_library context gives its identity. Select any relevant sections from one or several entries; pass the returned selection as launch_instructions in the child assignment. selected_launch_instructions contains exact sections already selected for this assignment. Instructions describe ways to work; they do not select resources, enable tools, override caller constraints, establish current availability or supply scientific evidence. Inventory and fresh observations remain separate. No instruction read or selection is mandatory.
